findings:
🟠 [v10-claim-rebuild-assert] MUST-FIX The v9→v10 migration rebuilds the claim table only when sqlite_master.sql lacks `group_id`, but the assertion at db.ts compares `before.n` (count on `claim`) to `after.n` (count on `claim_v10`). When migration runs a SECOND time after a prior successful v10, `claimRow.sql` already contains `group_id` so the block is skipped and idempotency holds — fine. However, on the very first run when claim already has rows, the CREATE TABLE for `claim_v10` declares `group_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'cookys'` but the column list in INSERT INTO claim_v10 does SELECT `team_id, claim_key, ...` which only has 7 columns before group_id; the literal `'cookys'` fills it. That works. But if `claim` happens to have no rows (fresh v9 path), `before.n===0===after.n` and we still drop+rename, which is fine. The real issue: the spec mandates an assertion comparing counts before/after; the current code reads `before` before any changes and `after` after the INSERT — correct. No concrete failure here, but the index `idx_claim_legacy_unique` is created UNCONDITIONALLY in the trailing `db.exec(...)` block AFTER the claim rebuild. On a v10 DB that already has claim_v10 shape, re-running the migration re-creates this index (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS — idempotent). However, this UNIQUE index on `(team_id, claim_key)` across groups is NOT specified in the plan §2.1.10; it changes claim semantics (v9 had unique constraint via PK only; adding a unique on (team_id, claim_key) across all groups prevents the same claim_key from existing in different groups, contradicting the new v10 PK of (team_id, group_id, claim_key) which deliberately scopes claims per-group). This is a concrete divergence from spec — smallest remediation: remove `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_claim_legacy_unique ON claim(team_id, claim_key);` from the trailing exec block in db.ts migrateV9ToV10. Impact: silently prevents v10 per-group claim uniqueness from ever being used, breaking the spec's claim PK design.
🟠 [backfill-not-guarded-by-team] MUST-FIX In db.ts migrateV9ToV10, the data backfill runs `INSERT INTO group_member SELECT ?, h.handle, ?, ?, '0' FROM human h WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM group_member gm WHERE gm.handle = h.handle)`. The spec requires the backfill to be gated by `SELECT 1 FROM schema_version WHERE version=10` absent AND by team membership (handle in `human` of `hangar`). The current WHERE clause omits `h.team_id=?` and `h.disabled_at IS NULL`, so humans from other teams (or disabled humans) would be admitted into cookys. Smallest remediation: change to `WHERE h.team_id=? AND h.disabled_at IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM group_member gm WHERE gm.handle = h.handle)` and pass HANGAR_TEAM_ID as a bind param. Impact: cross-team or disabled humans become cookys members — leaks authorization across teams and admits removed users.
🟠 [peers-file-legacy-strict-guard-bypass] MUST-FIX In peers-file.ts `computeStrictSignals`, the `enabled_human_not_in_default_group` query uses `gm.group_id=?` bound to DEFAULT_GROUP_ID but the subquery is correlated to `h.handle` only; it does not check that `gm.group_id='cookys'` for the SAME handle — it just asks "does ANY cookys member exist?" because the NOT EXISTS is correlated to outer handle but only checks group_id=cookys for that handle. Actually rereading: `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM group_member gm WHERE gm.group_id=? AND gm.handle=h.handle)` — this is correct: it checks that no row exists for (cookys, h.handle). However the guard uses `h.team_id=?` bound to HANGAR_TEAM_ID — correct. But it does NOT filter `h.disabled_at IS NULL` outside the NOT EXISTS — wait, the outer WHERE has `h.disabled_at IS NULL`. OK that part is correct. The actual bug: `default_membership_narrowed` uses `caps_json != ? OR since_msg_id != ?` with `since_msg_id` bound to `SINCE_ALL` ('0'). But after a legacy seedPeers backfills with `'0'` for since_msg_id — correct. However, `caps_json != ALL_MEMBER_CAPS` uses string equality; if SQLite stored JSON in a different whitespace (it doesn't, since we always JSON.stringify same array order), this is fine. No concrete failure. Removing this finding.
🟠 [seedPeers-strict-grown-double-count] MUST-FIX In peers-file.ts `computeDiff`, the loop over `after` adds a handle to `grown` both when the group is brand-new AND when the group existed but the member is new (the two branches are identical: `if (!beforeMembers?.has(handle) && !beforeGroups.has(group))` else `if (!beforeMembers?.has(handle))`). This is a logic no-op duplication, not a bug per se. But the `grown` list will include a member both when added to a brand-new group AND when added to an existing group — both paths emit the same `{handle, group}` entry once because the second `else if` is only reached when the first is false. Actually only ONE push happens per (group, handle). No concrete failure; removing.
🟠 [seedPeers-remove-handles-strict-mode-default-group] MUST-FIX In peers-file.ts strict-mode block, `DELETE FROM peer_group` for groups not in `desiredGroups` runs BEFORE the human revocation loop. If a vanished human was the only member of a removed group, the cascade `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `peer_group` → `group_member` would have already cleaned up — fine. But the revocation `DELETE FROM group_member WHERE handle=?` then runs against handles whose group memberships may already be gone via cascade — harmless. However, the test 'strict diff reports grown memberships' expects `diff.grown === [{handle:'c', group:'lab'}]` (single entry). With the current `computeDiff`, when c is added to lab (existing group, new member), the loop over `after` finds `lab` in `beforeGroups` AND `c` not in `beforeMembers` → pushes `{handle:'c', group:'lab'}`. The first branch `!beforeMembers?.has(handle) && !beforeGroups.has(group)` is false (group exists), the else-if `!beforeMembers?.has(handle)` is true → pushes once. Correct. No concrete failure. Removing this finding.
🟠 [store-grep-test-flaky] MUST-FIX In groups.test.ts, the grep test for `store.ts` slices function bodies by finding `\n  }` after the function name and then `\n  ` from there — this is a fragile heuristic. If any of the five `fetch*` functions ends with a single `}` (no preceding space-newline pattern) or the file uses tabs, the slice will be wrong and `.filter(` may not be detected even if present (false negative) OR the slice may include code from another function (false positive). Smallest remediation: replace body slicing with a regex match on `function fetchXxx( ... ) { ... }` using balanced-brace parsing, or skip the grep test entirely for P0 (spec lists it as MUST-PASS but it's a static guard, not a behavioral one). Impact: test passes today only by accident of formatting; if anyone reformats store.ts, the test silently breaks. Concrete failure mode: a future contributor adds `.filter(...)` inside fetchSince for valid reasons and this test misses it because the slice boundary is wrong, OR a `.filter(` call elsewhere gets caught inside the slice. The smallest concrete remediation is to use the actual existing `db.ts` body-slice idiom (count braces) — but for review, flag this as fragile and require a more robust body extractor.
🟠 [legacy-mode-caps-overwrite-blankets-all] MUST-FIX In peers-file.ts seedPeers legacy branch, after the backfill INSERT it runs `UPDATE group_member SET caps_json=? WHERE group_id=?` with ALL_MEMBER_CAPS and DEFAULT_GROUP_ID — this UNCONDITIONALLY overwrites every existing cookys member's caps_json to ALL_MEMBER_CAPS, even members that a prior strict seed had narrowed. Combined with the `computeStrictSignals` guard that throws when `default_membership_narrowed` is true, this means a legacy file can never be loaded on a strict-narrowed DB (guard catches it first — correct). But on a legacy-DB (caps already ALL), this UPDATE is a no-op. On the very first legacy load (fresh v10 DB, no existing group_member rows), the INSERT populates them and the UPDATE is a no-op. So in practice no destructive overwrite happens because the guard fires first. However, the UPDATE runs INSIDE the legacy branch even when the guard already threw — wait, the guard throw happens INSIDE the transaction at the top, before any writes. So the legacy UPDATE never executes when it would clobber. The concern is moot. Removing this finding — no concrete failure because the guard prevents the destructive path.
🟠 [reply_route-migration-no-column-backfill] MUST-FIX The v9→v10 migration adds `group_id` to `reply_route` via `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT 'cookys'` (gated by pragma check). Spec mandates this. Implemented correctly. No defect. Removing.
🟠 [reply-route-test-expects-column] The db.test.ts 'migrateV8ToV9' block expects `reply_route` columns to include `group_id` in a SPECIFIC position (`to_handle`, `group_id`, `to_filter_json`). This test now depends on the order of columns in the CREATE TABLE which only runs for fresh DBs. The migrateV8ToV9 test creates a v8 fixture (which does NOT have group_id) then opens, runs migration chain, and expects the resulting reply_route to have group_id in that exact position. But ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN appends to the end of the table, so after v9→v10 the reply_route column order for an upgraded DB would be `..., to_handle, to_filter_json, thread_root, ..., group_id` (at the end), NOT `to_handle, group_id, to_filter_json, ...`. The test asserts `cols.toEqual([..., 'to_handle', 'group_id', 'to_filter_json', ...])`. For a FRESH DB the CREATE TABLE in schema.sql has group_id in that exact position (between to_handle and to_filter_json) — so fresh passes. But the test uses `openDatabase(':memory:')` which creates a fresh DB — so fresh passes. However, the migrateV8ToV9 describe block earlier creates a v8 fixture file and upgrades it; the `cols` assertion runs against the upgraded DB which would NOT have group_id at that position. Looking again: the assertion is at line ~255 inside `it('a fresh DB ends at version 9 with all four tables + the correlation index', ...)` — uses `openDatabase(':memory:')` (fresh). So the assertion passes for fresh only. No concrete failure for P0. Removing this finding.
🟠 [migrateV9ToV10-via-export-only] The test imports `migrateV9ToV10` directly and calls it on a v9 fixture built inline. The exported function is NOT used by any application code in P0 (the spec says no route changes; the function is only called by openDatabase). The export is correct for testability. No defect.
🟠 [strict-cap-update-resets-watermark] In peers-file.ts strict branch, when an existing `group_member` row exists, only `caps_json` is UPDATEd; `since_msg_id` and `member_since` are preserved. Correct per spec. No defect.
🟠 [init-test-mode-assertion-order] init.test.ts adds `expect(r.mode).toBe('legacy')` and `expect(r.diff.mode).toBe('legacy')` after the existing seeded assertion. Correct per spec. No defect.
🟠 [shared-constants-ALL_MEMBER_CAPS-alias] `export const ALL_MEMBER_CAPS: readonly MemberCap[] = MEMBER_CAPS` — this is a reference alias, not a copy. The test asserts `ALL_MEMBER_CAPS === MEMBER_CAPS` (same reference) — passes. Correct. No defect.
🟠 [envelope-test-fast-check-arbitrary-update] The fast-check arbitrary adds `group: fc.constant(DEFAULT_GROUP_ID)` to envelope generation. Required because group is now required on Envelope (with default). Correct. No defect.
🔵 [idx_claim_legacy_unique-extra] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The `idx_claim_legacy_unique` UNIQUE index on `(team_id, claim_key)` added in db.ts migrateV9ToV10 contradicts the v10 PK `(team_id, group_id, claim_key)` which is intentionally per-group. This is an extra invariant the spec does not ask for. Remove from P0; revisit in P1 if cross-group claim_key uniqueness becomes a requirement. MUST-FIX (see above) takes priority; this CUT notes it can be dropped.
🔵 [seedPeers-grows-double-branch] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The two-branch `if/else if` in computeDiff for `grown` is a no-op duplicate. Collapse to single `if (!beforeMembers?.has(handle))`. Excluded from P0 minimal version since behavior is identical.
🔵 [store-grep-test-fragile-body-slice] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The `\n  }` / `\n  ` heuristic for slicing function bodies is fragile. Acceptable for P0 if all five fetch* helpers currently follow the exact 2-space-indent convention; defer robust brace-balancing extraction to a follow-up.
